entities.summary:
Count Anton Corfiz von Ulfeldt was an Austrian politician and diplomat of Danish descent who played a key role in the history of Europe during the 18th century. Born into a noble family, Ulfeldt was educated at the University of Copenhagen and later at the University of Vienna, where he studied law and philosophy. He served as a diplomat for the Danish royal family in various European courts, including the court of Empress Maria Theresa of Austria, and was appointed as the Danish ambassador to Austria in 1743. Ulfeldt's diplomatic efforts helped to secure a peace treaty between Denmark and Austria, which ended a long period of conflict between the two powers. He also played a role in the negotiation of the Treaty of Copenhagen, which established a new border between Denmark and Sweden. Ulfeldt's diplomatic career was marked by his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers, and he is remembered as one of the most important diplomats of his time. In 1769, Ulfeldt died at the age of 38, leaving behind a legacy as a skilled and influential diplomat who shaped the course of European history.

Ulfeldt's diplomatic career was influenced by the growing tensions between Denmark and Austria, which had been exacerbated by the War of the Austrian Succession. He was part of a group of Danish diplomats who worked to secure a peace treaty with Austria, which was negotiated in 1743. This treaty marked a significant turning point in the history of Denmark and Austria, and Ulfeldt's role in its negotiation helped to secure a lasting peace between the two powers.
